preamble: The alveolar nasal /n/ is realized as a voiced uvular nasal [ɴ] through regressive place assimilation: a syllable-final /n/ copies the place of a following uvular consonant. In Cusco Quechua a nasal assimilates to the place of a following obstruent, so /n/ before /q/ is [ɴ], as in /ˈtɑnqɑ-j/ [ˈtɑɴqɑ-j] '¡empuja!' and Peruvian Quechua sunqu [ˈs̠oɴqo] 'heart'.

examples.note: Rodríguez Champi (2006): a nasal assimilates to the place of a following obstruent, even across a word boundary.
Listed for Peruvian Quechua as an allophone of /n/.

context: Before uvular consonants (/q/ and its aspirated and ejective counterparts)
sources: Rodríguez Champi, A. (2006). Quechua de Cusco. Ilustraciones fonéticas de lenguas amerindias. http://lengamer.org/publicaciones/trabajos/quechua_cusco_afi.pdf
